text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Organized structure with clear introduction stating position, three body paragraphs each with a topic sentence (dangerous, cause problems, lazy), and a conclusion", "quality": "Organizational structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting point in its own paragraph with a logical progression to a conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Uses quoted evidence from the article such as \"when the vehicle is in danger of backing into an object\" and \"the technology fails and some is injured, who is at fault-the driver or the manufactuer?\"", "quality": "Evidence integration", "description": "The essay incorporates specific details and direct quotations from the source article to support its claims."}, {"evidence": "Develops each argument with explanation, such as explaining how lawsuits and lost business would follow from technology failures", "quality": "Elaboration of claims", "description": "The essay extends each point beyond a simple assertion by explaining consequences and reasoning behind the claims."}, {"evidence": "Coherent sentences and mostly standard spelling and grammar throughout, e.g., \"Having driverless cars is just more oppurtunity for us citizens to be able to wreck.\"", "quality": "Conventional control", "description": "The essay maintains readable, mostly grammatical prose that allows the argument to be followed without decoding errors."}, {"evidence": "Rhetorical questions and direct address like \"are we really so lazy that we can't get in the car and simply drive a few blocks to the grocery store\"", "quality": "Rhetorical engagement", "description": "The essay uses rhetorical devices to engage the reader and reinforce its persuasive points."}]}
